title: Python Developer
summary: Python from first principles through to a tested command-line tool and a small web API — plus the surrounding practice (virtual environments, dependencies, packaging) that tutorials skip. The shortest route from here into the AI and data tracks.
twoHundredKPotential: Not from this path on its own, and anyone telling you otherwise is selling something. This path is about becoming employable and genuinely useful. The senior and architect tracks on this platform are where the higher bands live, and they assume the ground this course covers.
salarySource: Aggregated public US entry-level ranges (Glassdoor, Indeed, Levels.fyi, BLS occupational data). Estimates only — update via Admin.
demandNotes: Python is the default language of data work, automation and the entire AI toolchain. Its ceiling as a standalone skill is modest; its value as the entry point to better-paid data and AI work is high, and that is the honest reason to learn it.
aiRiskNotes: Short Python scripts are the single thing code models write best, so “I can write a script” is no longer a job. “I can build a tool that survives bad input, is tested, and someone else can install and run” still is. This path is built around that difference.
responsibilities: Write readable Python that uses the standard library rather than reaching for a package first
Build command-line tools and small web APIs that other people can install and run
Handle malformed input and failure explicitly instead of letting exceptions escape
Manage dependencies and virtual environments so the project is reproducible
Write pytest tests, including for the failure paths
Use type hints to make the intent of a function readable without running it
interviewFocus: What is the difference between a list and a generator, and when does it matter?
Explain mutable default arguments and why they bite people
What does a virtual environment actually do?
How would you process a file larger than available memory?
What is the GIL and when should you care about it?
Show me how you would test a function that calls an external API

title: Front-End Web Developer
summary: HTML, CSS, JavaScript and TypeScript learned properly before a framework hides them: layout, the DOM, async data, types and accessibility. The prerequisite for the Angular and full-stack work the senior tracks assume.
twoHundredKPotential: Not from this path on its own, and anyone telling you otherwise is selling something. This path is about becoming employable and genuinely useful. The senior and architect tracks on this platform are where the higher bands live, and they assume the ground this course covers.
salarySource: Aggregated public US entry-level ranges (Glassdoor, Indeed, Levels.fyi, BLS occupational data). Estimates only — update via Admin.
demandNotes: The most crowded entry point in software, and the one where a bootcamp portfolio no longer distinguishes anyone. Demand is real but the competition is heavy — which is why this path pushes accessibility, performance and TypeScript rather than another landing page.
aiRiskNotes: The honest assessment on this list. Generating a component from a description is the strongest thing current models do, and straightforward markup work is genuinely being absorbed. What is not: accessibility that survives audit, performance work on a real device, and design judgement. Treat this path as a foundation to build on, not a destination.
responsibilities: Build responsive layouts with flexbox and grid that hold up at phone width
Write semantic, accessible markup that works with a keyboard and a screen reader
Consume REST APIs and handle loading, empty, error and success states explicitly
Use TypeScript to make data shapes explicit instead of hoping
Debug in browser dev tools: the network panel, the element inspector, the console
Keep pages fast on a mid-range phone, not only on a developer laptop
interviewFocus: Explain the box model and what box-sizing: border-box changes
What is the event loop, and why does a long synchronous function freeze the page?
How do you make a custom control keyboard accessible?
What is the difference between == and === and why does it matter?
Walk me through what happens between typing a URL and seeing the page
How would you find out why a page is slow on a mid-range phone?
